cim_eredeti: Understanding Artificial Intelligence: What to Watch and Learn
szoveg_eredeti:
Artificial intelligence is changing everything: how we learn, how we work and how we connect with each other. As AI becomes more integrated into our daily routines, it raises important questions about its impact on our communities, the opportunities it creates and the challenges it presents.

If you want to learn more about AI but don’t know where to start, you’re not alone. Explore these documentaries, local reporting and educational resources from Nebraska Public Media and PBS to better understand how artificial intelligence works and how it's shaping our world.

As AI becomes woven into daily life, Americans face a choice: control the technology or be controlled by it. The latest episode of Breaking the Deadlock, a groundbreaking public affairs series from PBS, tackles the ethical challenges raised by artificial intelligence,

Through a series of hypothetical dilemmas, leaders in tech, culture, politics and journalism debate AI’s ethical challenges, seeking not consensus, but a shared understanding of what’s at stake. It’s a fast-paced one-hour journey with moderator Aaron Tang guiding panelists through complex hypothetical scenarios.

Breaking the Deadlock: AI: Who’s in Control is available to stream on PBS.org, the PBS app and YouTube.

What ideas shaped AI technology before it entered our everyday lives? How is artificial intelligence affected by human history, politics and cultural powers that came before it? And what ideas are driving the global AI boom?

The documentary Independent Lens: Ghost in the Machine examines these questions and more as it reveals how the human values, biases and power structures behind artificial intelligence are shaping our world—and its societal and environmental consequences.

Ghost in the Machine premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival and is part of the most recent season of Independent Lens, the award-winning public television documentary series. You can watch Ghost in the Machine on PBS.org, the PBS app, or YouTube.

Earlier this year, Nebraska Public Media News examined how artificial intelligence is impacting classrooms across Nebraska, from kindergarten through higher education. This series by education reporter Jolie Peal explored several areas of AI in education, including school policies on AI, how educational institutions are implementing the technology and the safety concerns around it.

For teens (and adults!) who want to learn more about AI, check out the PBS LearningMedia series Crash Course: Artificial Intelligence. This quick-paced, imaginative series is aimed at learners of all ages. Over the course of 20 short videos, the show explains what AI is, how it is created and trained, and how humans can use AI—for example, how platforms like Netflix and YouTube use AI algorithms to recommend content to viewers.

PBS LearningMedia collects educational materials related to AI, including clips from PBS News Hour, Nova and the PBS KIDS series Ruff Ruffman: Humble Media Genius. You can filter the collection by grade level and resource type to find the best resources for your needs.
